title: Processes
locators: Printed pp22-23: interruption and structured stages
assumptions: Author's process/event distinction and proposed persistence account.
conclusion: Interruption alone leaves a structured-stage alternative; a separate argument addresses persistence.
proof_status: Selected full-text argument inspected; its metaphysics is contested, not accepted as a theorem.
open_questions: Whether an independently defended organizing account defeats the further persistence argument.
relevance: Exact predecessor for the interruption test and its limited reach.
limits: Not a growing-block argument or a full temporal-inventory comparison; no cover-to-cover audit claimed.

title: Processes, Continuants, and Individuals
version: Author upload dated 15 July 2016, manuscript referring to Mind122(487),781-812(2013), DOI10.1093/mind/fzt080; manuscript pagination differs from print
assumptions: Distinguishes process individuation, temporal parts and essential membership.
conclusion: Defends form-based modal robustness; distinguishes happening from whole presence.
proof_status: Selected full-text passages directly read; the whole metaphysical account and later applications were not audited.
dependencies: The author's event/process terminology and identity criteria
open_questions: What independently fixes organizing form and strict cross-world identity?
relevance: Supplies a stronger process alternative and an exact predecessor to the project's occurrence-presence criticism.
limits: Transcription of author-uploaded text, not a page-image check of print. Does not prove a growing or eternal inventory. Note18 expressly allows rejecting event essentialism.

title: Processes, Continuants and Individuals

title: No Chance for the Change Argument – A Reply to Stout’s “The Category of Occurrent Continuants”
version: CEUR-WS Vol2518, paper-FOUST1, copyright2019; 9-page PDF; distinct from the later Dialectica reply
locators: Sections2-4, PDFpp2-6; stated interpretation of the change constraint and competing truth conditions
assumptions: Examines Stout's change argument and its claimed neutrality between persistence theories.
conclusion: Author challenges its validity/neutrality; not a general refutation of process realism.
proof_status: Selected full-text argument read; later objection section and conclusion not fully audited.
dependencies: Readings of change, persistence and temporal predication
open_questions: How much of the disagreement concerns intended interpretation rather than a shared premise?
relevance: Independent warning against importing the disputed persistence account into the comparison.
limits: No full source audit of Stout2016 performed through this reply. Not the later published reply version.
